title: Choroidal Melanoma: A Comprehensive Clinical Guide
summary: Choroidal melanoma is the most common primary intraocular malignancy in adults, arising from melanocytes within the uveal tract. Early detection via clinical markers is essential for systemic prognosis and vision preservation.

sections.title: Disease Overview
sections.content: Choroidal melanoma is a malignant tumor arising from the melanocytes of the uveal tract. It represents approximately 80% of all uveal melanomas and is recognized as the most common primary intraocular cancer found in the adult population.

sections.title: Predisposing Risk Factors
content: Fair skin and light eye color (Blue/Green)

content.explanation: T: Thickness > 2 mm; F: Fluid (subretinal); S: Symptoms (blurred vision/flashes); O: Orange pigment (lipofuscin); M: Margin within 3 mm of optic disc; U: Ultrasound (acoustic hollowness); HH: Halo absence; D: Drusen absence.

rows: Acoustic hollowness, choroidal excavation, and 'collar-button' (mushroom) shape.
Double circulation pattern (simultaneous retinal and tumor vessel filling).
Documentation of pigmentation (melanotic vs. amelanotic) and borders.

sections.title: CRITICAL WARNING SIGNS
content: Rapid growth of a documented pre-existing nevus
Presence of Sentinel Vessels (dilated episcleral vessels)
Extraocular extension through the scleral emissary channels
Diffuse growth pattern (higher risk of delayed diagnosis)

sections.title: Management Pathway
content: Step 1: Observation for small, low-risk, dormant lesions.
Step 2: Radiation Therapy (Plaque Brachytherapy or Proton Beam).
Step 3: Surgical Enucleation for large tumors or blind/painful eyes.
Step 4: Systemic Surveillance for hepatic metastasis.
